title: Imports: Graph Theory and Set Theory
content: Imports Mathlib's `SimpleGraph` for graph infrastructure, `Cardinal` for uncountable cardinals ($\aleph_1$), and `Set.Countable` for the countability predicate. This combination bridges finite combinatorics (graph coloring, paths) with infinite set theory (uncountable cardinals, countable sets).
mathContext: Uses $\texttt{SimpleGraph}$ for undirected graphs, $\texttt{Cardinal}$ for $\aleph_0, \aleph_1$, and $\texttt{Set.Countable}$ for the predicate distinguishing countable from uncountable vertex sets.

title: Paths in Graphs
content: Defines a path as a list of vertices where consecutive entries are adjacent. This concrete representation (rather than Mathlib's `Walk` type) allows direct reasoning about internal vertices via list operations, which is essential for defining internal disjointness.
mathContext: A path $p = (v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_k)$ satisfies $v_i \sim v_{i+1}$ for all $0 \leq i < k$. The internal vertices are $\{v_1, \ldots, v_{k-1}\}$.

title: Internal Disjointness of Paths
content: Two paths are internally disjoint if they share no internal vertices (vertices that are neither first nor last). A collection of paths is pairwise internally disjoint if every pair is internally disjoint. This is the key concept for Menger's theorem: $k$-connectivity is equivalent to $k$ pairwise internally disjoint paths between any two vertices.
mathContext: Paths $p_1, p_2$ from $u$ to $v$ are internally disjoint iff $\text{int}(p_1) \cap \text{int}(p_2) = \emptyset$ where $\text{int}(p) = p \setminus \{u, v\}$. By Menger's theorem (1927), $\kappa(u,v) = $ max number of pairwise internally disjoint $u$-$v$ paths.

title: Infinite Vertex-Connectivity
content: A graph is infinitely connected if any two distinct vertices are joined by infinitely many pairwise internally disjoint paths. This is an extremely strong structural property: by the infinite Menger theorem (Aharoni-Berger, 2009), it is equivalent to saying no finite vertex cut can disconnect the graph.
mathContext:
$$G \text{ is } \infty\text{-connected} \iff \forall u \neq v,\; \exists \text{ infinitely many pairwise internally disjoint } u\text{-}v \text{ paths}$$
By the infinite Menger theorem: $\kappa(u,v) = \aleph_0$ for all $u \neq v$, equivalently no finite vertex cut separates any two vertices.

title: Chromatic Number ≥ ℵ₁
content: Defines $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$ via the negation of countable colorability: no function $c : V \to C$ with $C$ countable can be a proper coloring. By the De Bruijn-Erdős theorem (1951), this implies finite subgraphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number.
mathContext:
$$\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1 \iff \forall C \text{ countable},\; \forall c : V \to C,\; \exists u \sim v : c(u) = c(v)$$
By De Bruijn-Erdős, $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$ implies $\chi(G) \geq k$ for every finite $k$.

title: Induced Subgraph on a Vertex Set
content: Constructs the induced subgraph $G[S]$ on a vertex set $S$: vertices are elements of $S$, edges are inherited from $G$. The `SimpleGraph` axioms (symmetry, no loops) are verified by delegating to $G$. This is the key construction for Problem 1068: we seek a countable $S$ such that $G[S]$ is infinitely connected.
mathContext: $G[S]$ has vertex set $S$ and edge set $\{(u,v) : u, v \in S,\, u \sim_G v\}$. The problem asks: $\exists S \subseteq V$ countable such that $G[S]$ is $\infty$-connected.

title: Erdős Problem 1068: The Main Conjecture
content: The central open question: does every graph with $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$ contain a countable vertex set $S$ such that $G[S]$ is infinitely connected? This is a weakening of Problem 1067 (disproved by Soukup). The restriction to countable subgraphs makes this fundamentally different — Soukup's counterexample controls uncountable sets but says nothing about countable ones.
mathContext: $$\forall G \text{ with } \chi(G) \geq \aleph_1,\; \exists S \subseteq V(G) : |S| \leq \aleph_0 \wedge G[S] \text{ is } \infty\text{-connected}$$

title: Soukup's Counterexample (2015)
content: Soukup (2015, *Combinatorica*) constructed in ZFC a graph with $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$ where every uncountable vertex set induces a graph that is NOT infinitely connected. The construction uses ladder systems on non-special trees: pairs of vertices from any uncountable set can be separated by a finite vertex cut. This makes the countable case (Problem 1068) the remaining open question.
mathContext:
$$\exists G : \chi(G) \geq \aleph_1 \wedge \forall S \subseteq V(G),\; |S| > \aleph_0 \implies G[S] \text{ is NOT } \infty\text{-connected}$$
Soukup's graph uses $\omega_1$-trees with ladder systems defining edges.

title: Problem 1067 Disproved
content: Problem 1067 asked whether every graph with $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$ contains an infinitely connected subgraph with $\chi \geq \aleph_1$. Soukup showed the answer is NO. Problem 1068 weakens this by dropping the chromatic number requirement and only asking for countability of the subgraph.
mathContext:
Problem 1067 (DISPROVED): $\forall G$ with $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$, $\exists H \subseteq G$ with $H$ $\infty$-connected and $\chi(H) \geq \aleph_1$.
Problem 1068 (OPEN): replace $\chi(H) \geq \aleph_1$ with $|V(H)| \leq \aleph_0$.

title: No Finite Vertex Separator
content: In an infinitely connected graph, removing any finite set of vertices leaves any two remaining vertices connected. This is a consequence of the infinite Menger theorem (Aharoni-Berger, 2009, *Inventiones mathematicae*), which resolved the Erdős-Menger conjecture: in infinite graphs, the max number of disjoint $A$-$B$ paths equals the min size of an $A$-$B$ separator.
mathContext: If $G$ is $\infty$-connected and $S$ is finite with $u, v \notin S$, then $\exists$ $u$-$v$ path in $G - S$. Follows from $\kappa(u,v) = \aleph_0 > |S|$.

title: Set-Theoretic Sensitivity
content: Komjáth (2013, *Israel J. Math.*) showed that a related question (graphs of cardinality $\aleph_1$ with $\chi \geq \aleph_1$ and uncountable infinitely connected subgraphs) is independent of ZFC. Problem 1068 may also be sensitive to set-theoretic axioms, though independence has not been established for this specific variant. Recorded here as documentation prose (no formal declaration).
mathContext: Komjáth's independence result uses forcing: in one model of ZFC the answer is yes, in another no. The ZFC-independence status of Problem 1068 specifically remains unknown.

title: Bowler-Pikhurko Simplification (2024)
content: Bowler and Pikhurko (2024) provided a simplified construction of Soukup's counterexample for Problem #1067, illuminating the structure of the problem; their construction uses tree-like "ladder" graphs. Recorded here as documentation prose (no formal declaration).
mathContext: The simplified construction (arXiv:2402.05984) replaces Soukup's non-special tree technique with a more direct ladder-graph approach, preserving the key property that uncountable vertex sets have finite vertex cuts.

title: Structural Implications of Infinite Connectivity
content: Two fully proved (non-axiomatized) theorems: (1) `inf_connected_implies_path`: infinite connectivity implies the existence of a path between any two distinct vertices (extracting one path from the infinite family), and (2) `inf_connected_subgraph_has_paths`: if $G[S]$ is infinitely connected, then any two vertices in $S$ are path-connected within $S$. These are verified by Lean's kernel.
mathContext: $\infty$-connected $\implies$ connected: the infinite family of disjoint paths is nonempty, yielding at least one $u$-$v$ path. For induced subgraphs: $G[S]$ $\infty$-connected $\implies$ $G[S]$ connected.
